conventions.convention: A₀ = Q[q]_(q), with uniformizer q, residue field Q, fraction field Q(q), and ord_q(q) = 1.
Weight spaces are chosen P-label spaces; integrability means vectorwise local nilpotence of both E_i and F_i, without finite-dimensionality, bounded support, or uniform nilpotence.
Divided powers use symmetric quantum factorials. In module string expansions, coefficients beyond the string bottom must be zero.
The negative-half projector uses ordinary powers of e_i', with coefficient (−1)^m q_i^(−m(m−1)/2) F_i^(m); its coefficients are not divided derivation powers.
The tensor coproduct is ΔE_i = E_i ⊗ K_i⁻¹ + 1 ⊗ E_i and ΔF_i = F_i ⊗ 1 + K_i ⊗ F_i. Lowering selects the first factor for φ_i(first) > ε_i(second); raising selects it for φ_i(first) ≥ ε_i(second).
A crystal basis is an unsigned Q-basis of L/qL, graded and operator-stable, with the partial inverse equivalence f̃_i b = b′ iff b = ẽ_i b′.
For module crystals, ε_i and φ_i are finite raising and lowering lengths. For B(∞), ε_i is finite, φ_i = ε_i + ⟨h_i,wt⟩ is formal and may be negative, and the actual lowering length is infinite.

Highest-weight projection commutes with lowering on every residue, but raising compatibility is asserted only when the projected residue survives. The basis bijection is restricted to surviving residues.

The module polarization is σ-contravariant, whereas the half polarization has F_i adjoint to e_i'. The large-weight comparison has module constant term C_ν times the half pairing, where C_ν = ∏_i(1−q_i²)^(−ν_i), congruent to 1 modulo q.

The grand loop conservatively retains AC inherited from the negative-half field-form supplier; finite component bases, their uniquely determined duals, and Gram inversion require no additional simultaneous choice.

load_bearing.statement: For every integer r ≥ 0, the interlocking clauses A(r)–O(r) hold. Consequently (𝓛(λ),𝓑(λ)) is a crystal basis of V(λ), its weight ranks equal the corresponding crystal cardinalities, and the module and negative-half lattice components are free over A₀.

In a chosen P-graded type-one module with E_i and F_i locally nilpotent, every u ∈ M_λ has a unique finite admissible expansion u = ∑_n F_i^(n)u_n, with u_n ∈ ker(E_i) ∩ M_(λ+nα_i) and u_n = 0 when n > ⟨λ+nα_i,h_i⟩. Highest spaces of negative coroot weight vanish; their divided strings are injective through the bottom and zero afterward.

P_i projects U_q⁻ onto ker e_i' along F_iU_q⁻. Every element has a unique finite expansion ∑_n F_i^(n)u_n with u_n ∈ ker e_i' and u_n = q_i^(n(n−1)/2)P_i(e_i')^n u. Its string shifts satisfy ẽ_i f̃_i = id, ker ẽ_i = ker e_i', and injectivity of f̃_i; the projector and coefficients preserve U_A⁻.

For simple rank-one modules V(a), V(b), with a,b ≥ 0 and the stated coproduct, the product divided-basis A₀-lattice is a crystal lattice. Modulo q, lowering changes the first position when a−j > k and the second otherwise; raising changes the first when a−j ≥ k and the second otherwise. The resulting chains partition the divided rectangle and satisfy partial inverses.

A crystal lattice is a free, generating, weight-graded A₀-submodule stable under both Kashiwara operators. A crystal basis adds a graded Q-basis of L/qL stable under both induced operators up to zero and satisfying their partial-inverse equivalence; the negative-half version uses root grading.

For dominant λ,μ, the cyclic tensor highest summand is V(λ+μ). The prescribed grading-preserving maps Φ and Ψ satisfy ΨΦ = id and are adjoint for the contravariant product form, with Φ an isometry. The prescribed second-top extraction S is U_q⁻-linear, and SΦ is the unique U_q⁻-linear surjection sending the highest vector to v_λ.

For every dominant λ and root degree α, π_λ maps 𝓛(∞)_(−α) onto 𝓛(λ)_(λ−α), commutes with lowering modulo q, commutes with raising on surviving crystal residues, and bijects surviving residues onto 𝓑(λ)_(λ−α). For sufficiently large λ, the fixed-degree lattice and residue maps are isomorphisms.

The respective normalized polarizations of the highest-module and negative-half Kashiwara lattices are A₀-valued with orthonormal crystal residues. Every finite component pairing is perfect and self-dual, and 𝓛 = {x : ⟨x,x⟩ ∈ A₀} inside its field extension, retaining the field-half supplier's inherited AC hypothesis.

(𝓛(∞),𝓑(∞)) is a root-graded crystal basis of U_q⁻, with free component rank equal to its field dimension and crystal cardinality. Its highest-weight projections have the stated surviving-residue compatibility, and every lowering iterate is nonzero; ε_i is finite and φ_i is formal.

alerts.finding: F3 says “the map on residues is the crystal bijection onto 𝓑(λ) ∪ {0}.” The cited projection lemma, clause (c), bijects only surviving residues onto 𝓑(λ). The unrestricted map is not injective: in rank one, b_(m+1) and b_(m+2) both project to zero, as computed in ex-projection-from-b-infinity-to-a-highest-weight-crystal. Proof 1.1 correctly uses the surviving correspondence, so this appears to be a wording defect in F3.

F3 says “the highest-weight projection is compatible with the crystal operators modulo q” without the supplier's restriction on raising. The cited projection lemma, clause (b), asserts raising compatibility only for surviving residues; rank-one b_(m+1) violates unrestricted raising compatibility. The displayed proof uses half-lattice stability rather than raising through a killed projection, but the citation should retain its qualification.

F4 says π_λ carries 𝓛(∞) onto 𝓛(λ) “compatibly with the crystal operators modulo q,” omitting the surviving-residue restriction for raising in the cited projection lemma. The rank-one killed residue b_(m+1) is an explicit counterexample to unrestricted raising compatibility. The subsequent argument uses lowering and surviving tops; the concern is the unqualified supplier summary.

F5 correctly restricts its displayed bijection to π_λ(b) ≠ 0, but then describes it as “compatible with the crystal operators modulo q” without stating that raising compatibility is limited to surviving residues. The cited projection lemma includes that limitation, and ex-projection-from-b-infinity-to-a-highest-weight-crystal exhibits failure at b_(m+1). The proof distinguishes killed and surviving images; this is a citation-qualification concern.

seams_checked.note: The assigned items preserve the chosen label grading, symmetric divided powers, ordinary-power skew projector, universal highest-weight presentation, distinct module/half forms, and declared inherited AC. No integral freeness or A-valuedness stronger than the suppliers is imported.

The citing clauses retain admissible finite strings, the strict lowering/non-strict raising tie convention, crystal partial inverses, and grand-loop highest-weight bases. Module tensor and dual constructions explicitly exclude the negative half's formal φ_i convention.

Ranks, rational crystal bases, norm characterization, and componentwise A₀ perfection are faithfully imported; integral balancedness is established downstream. Four supplier summaries have the projection wording issues routed in alerts: three omit the raising-survival qualification, and one calls the map including killed residues a bijection.
